A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same iterative-denoising research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching ID in v1 to SID in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original graph-generation experiments on QM9, ZINC250k, Planar, and SBM, including controlled denoiser comparisons and an NFE ablation.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experimental results in Section 5 and Appendix F, alongside separately attributed external baseline results.

M1.justification: ID is renamed SID, but conditional-independent noising, predict-and-renoise sampling, training objectives, GNN architecture, and Critic-guided remasking remain unchanged. Equation corrections formalize the already described procedure rather than introduce a new algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same molecular and generic graph-generation tasks on QM9, ZINC250k, Planar, and SBM. Newly mentioning molecular scaffold extension does not establish an evaluated additional task.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain GDSS, DruM, DiGress, marginal and mask DDM, and the same proposed variants. Newly discussed planning methods are related work, not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Data splits, preprocessing, metrics, sample counts, model configurations, and the six-point NFE grid are retained. Both use 500 generation steps for the main experiments and report external baselines using 1000. New architecture disclosures do not establish changed experimental settings.

E4.justification: The controlled denoiser comparisons and ZINC250k NFE ablation test the same questions. The new process illustration and architecture-based cost discussion add explanation, without an additional ablation, robustness test, error analysis, or empirical case study.

E5.justification: Both versions report five sampling runs and appendix standard deviations. No new seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: v2 Figure 5 corrects the swapped Marginal DDM and ID curve assignments in v1 Figure 4's NSPDK and FCD plots. For example, at NFE 16, NSPDK 47.22 belongs to DDM and 27.86 to ID/SID, as the tables already indicated. All corresponding numerical result tables remain unchanged; this is a reporting correction, not a performance gain.

T1.justification: Appendix A.3 repairs the denoising derivation's summation variables and mixture expansion. Appendix A.4 replaces the probability-only objective with logarithmic binary-classification terms and the appropriate minimization argument. Equation 12 also explicitly conditions clean prediction on the corruption indicator. The central assumptions, propositions, and optimal-Critic formula remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: mitigating compounding errors through conditional independence, adding a Critic, improving graph generation, and reducing required sampling steps. The new contribution list consolidates existing claims.

C2.justification: New Appendix E.3 acknowledges approximately doubled training and inference cost from the Critic and discusses architectural cost differences with DruM. The expanded discussion identifies dense pairwise computations as a scalability limitation and suggests scaffold extension as a potential application. These are additional interpretations and qualifications, not measured runtime results.

D1.justification: v1 promises code release upon acceptance; v2 reports a public repository address. v2 also names the computing clusters and adds layer-count and edge-width comparisons with DruM in Table 5. Existing implementation, hyperparameter, and preprocessing documentation is retained; repository availability was not independently verified.

R1.justification: Section 2.5 substantially expands positioning against corrector sampling, confidence-based unmasking, and learned planning, emphasizing CID's operation on fully denoised predictions. New connections include Cold Diffusion, MaskGIT, planned denoising, and masked language diffusion. The graph-generation review is also expanded beyond its relocated v1 counterpart.

P1.justification: v2 broadly edits the abstract, introduction, background, method explanations, and evaluation narrative. It changes the title and ID/SID terminology, adds an explicit contribution list and dedicated related-work subsections, and introduces a comparative appendix. These constitute substantial editorial restructuring despite stable methods and experiments.

P2.justification: v2 adds the method-comparison Table 3, architecture-comparison Table 5, and process-illustration Figure 4. It redraws dependency diagrams and NFE plots, using logarithmic NFE spacing and corrected curve attribution, and compacts appendix tables. Existing benchmark-table structures and generated-sample galleries are largely retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reliability by correcting NFE curve attribution and repairing the optimal-Critic derivation, while clearer positioning, illustrations, and reported public code access improve usability. These are meaningful refinements to the same empirical study. The improvement remains limited by unresolved inequalities between Lemma 4.3 and Appendix A.5, and unfinished reviewer-response prose in the new computational-cost discussion.
